description: Solo-maintainer setup: one batched run per week, no automerge, majors only on request.

Only image and action versions are managed here. npm dependencies are deliberately left out: eight lockfiles would drown the dashboard, and their versions are already pinned by lockfiles that CI installs with `npm ci`.

kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager has no default file patterns; without this it would never look at redis:7-alpine or any other image tag in the manifests.

packageRules.description: Engine binaries ship under mutable tags (pavlof01/v8-d8:latest, pavlof01/jsc:debug, ...), so the tag alone says nothing about what a build used. Pinning the digest is what makes an engine image reproducible; Renovate then moves the digest deliberately instead of a rebuild silently picking up a new binary.
Routine image moves (including digest refreshes) land as a single PR per week.
Same for the actions used by the deploy and CI workflows.
Majors (node 22 -> 24, redis 7 -> 8, actions v4 -> v5) change runtime behaviour and are worth a deliberate look, so they wait on the dependency dashboard instead of opening PRs on their own.
Actions move in their own weekly group, pinned to commit SHAs by the preset above — a tag like v4 is mutable and can be repointed by a compromised action repo.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes are not worth holding for the weekly slot.
